findings.title: The complete comparison is still running
findings.detail: All 70 settings remain in the four-task comparison. Pending entries are not failures, and the small pilot is not used to rule out methods.

findings.title: Recovery can coexist with incorrect prose
findings.detail: Audited readouts recover required names, numbers or relations while also adding wrong details. The recovery endpoints measure narrower successes than complete explanation accuracy.

findings.title: Shortening trades information for simplicity
findings.detail: Deleting or filtering text can remove unsupported details and clarify extraction. It can also remove every useful reading site for a question.

selection.finding: Additional samples sometimes recover missing names or a clearer direction of action. Selected arithmetic hits can still describe the wrong calculation, and other useful details are lost.
selection.limits: These are illustrative cases, not an estimate of how often the changes occur. Complete sampling curves remain the quantitative comparison.

consensus.finding: Repetition can concentrate useful content, but repeated instructions and final-answer fragments also survive. Stricter filters can delete every useful reading site for a question.
consensus.limits: Repeated does not mean correct. Some numerical improvements come from emphasizing a number already present, rather than adding a faithful explanation.

pruning.finding: Removing bullets can delete an unsupported detail or remove competing numbers. It can also delete the only useful name or number. Several apparent improvements over one sample were already present in the selected parent.
pruning.limits: Separate parent comparisons are audited. A lower reconstruction contribution does not establish that a bullet is false; shorter text can change the judge's extraction.

pooling.finding: Combining original bullets can recover complementary names and relations. It can also put opposing directions, incompatible names or incorrect operations in the same readout.
pooling.limits: A correct recovered concept does not make the combined explanation coherent. The natural output lengths are retained in the comparison.

verification.finding: Comparing activation scores changes which descriptions are selected. The audited examples still include incorrect surrounding names and equations, even when the required concept is recovered.
verification.limits: The likelihood examples in this first pack cover arithmetic only. Full-bank scores are still pending for the other tasks; reconstruction and likelihood are evidence signals, not truth checks.

editing.finding: The first-round proposals have been generated. Their reconstruction scoring and final benchmark evaluation are still running.
editing.limits: No expanded editing result is claimed in this snapshot. New wording needs its own reconstruction vectors and separate evaluation.

combinations.finding: Some selected-and-pruned outputs retain a useful name while dropping another. Parent comparisons distinguish the effect of choosing a candidate from the additional effect of deleting bullets.
combinations.limits: The new pooled and repetition-weighted combinations are still running. They remain in the menu regardless of their eventual measured quality.
